title: Requires Any Role
prompt: A TypeScript route guard receives the current user roles and the roles allowed for a route. Write a function that returns true when the user has at least one allowed role.

explanation.beginner: Start by identifying what the function receives and what it must return. For Requires Any Role, read the story as a simple input-to-output rule: A TypeScript route guard receives the current user roles and the roles allowed for a route. Write a function that returns true when the user has at least one allowed role. Work through one small example by hand, then write the steps in TypeScript using plain variables before worrying about making the code shorter.
explanation.junior: Treat this as a small pure TypeScript function: avoid mutating inputs unless the prompt explicitly asks for it, return the requested shape exactly, and let the tests drive the edge cases. The main practice area is typescript, sets and authorization. Pay attention to edge cases and keep the transformation predictable as the input grows.
